event.value: Rehafted his axe without comment. He praised her 'steadfast service to the cause'; she quoted six coppers and went back to the anvil. He maintains his kit properly — she judges the work, not the worker, and the work is the only thing of his she respects.

He brought a snapped goblin hinge charm in as a 'dark shard'. Cold-set, no seam — better work than his. It did not go back into his hand; it went into the bench drawer she keeps for Joren Pell's identifications, to go home mended.

notes: Modeled at the EARLY stage: curt service, everything said through the work — her flaw is that she says almost nothing with her mouth, so the protagonist has never once understood her. Respect 5 is strictly professional (he cares for his tools); affection 0 because there is no warmth channel at all. Escalation per profile: mid-arc she names the maker's technique of every piece he broke; late-runs she tells him, once per visit, what came through the drawer this month — 'That's the whole conversation.' Boundary ahead and load-bearing: she will not unmake — no reforging a charm into a blade — and the day he sets a memorial-lamp fragment on her anvil and says 'make it kill better' is her breaking point. The mended-charms drawer is behavior, not a tracked fact; keep it out of dialogue he could overhear. Deltas sum to current dimensions.
